correctness.rationale: A finite total preorder has mutually accessible equivalence clusters arranged linearly; forth maps each source cluster to a single target cluster and induces a monotone sequence. Global onto makes this a nondecreasing surjection on cluster indices, determined by unique contiguous cuts e_0=0<e_1<⋯<e_k=h. Back at a point in the last source cluster assigned to target B_j forces images of that final cluster onto ALL of B_j; conversely endpoint surjectivity over each target B_j covers every target successor of every source point, giving pointwise f[R(x)]=S[f(x)]. Therefore labeled counts are ∑cuts∏ b_j^{sum earlier a_i}U(a_ej,b_j). Two-sided source/target within-cluster symmetric actions classify exactly the unordered multisets of fiber-column vectors with fixed row sums and positive final row, giving the coefficient product and existence iff a_ej≥b_j. Independently brute-forced all onto functions in 395 composition pairs, 1,550 valid maps and 247 orbit profiles with direct relation equality; separately reviewed the repository group-action script constructing actual source and target transposition orbits for 22 representative cases. Verified (a,b)=((2,2,2),(2,2)) gives 32 maps/4 orbits and ((3,2,3),(2,2)) gives 240/5. The finite enumeration corroborates, not proves, the arbitrary-cluster formulas.

evidence: Shapirovsky Proposition 3.4 permits lifting componentwise p-morphisms but does not enumerate all maps or give last-source-cluster necessary condition and two-sided orbit counts.

The published weak-order theorem counts arbitrary monotone maps of antichain levels by a two-state recurrence; its relation is not reflexive equivalence inside clusters and has no bounded-morphism back.
broader_coverage.reasoning: Neither the general modal preservation machinery nor the weak-order transfer recurrence logically yields the given S4.3 all-parameter orbit theorem; a specialized result about S4.3 morphisms could still dominate.

value.rationale: Finite linear preorders are the natural frames for S4.3, and globally surjective bounded morphisms preserve modal truths. The last-source-cluster constraint gives a sharp existence boundary and an exact complete classification of both labeled maps and quotient types under the two full frame symmetry groups. This is a coherent invariant and enumeration for all positive cluster vectors, with no requirement of a downstream general theorem.
